title: 690.  A Murderous Affair: Death at Mayerling (Part 2)

sentences.en: This episode is brought to you by the Lloyd's 5K House Deposit, and this is something that was last seen in 1996.
sentences.zh: 本期节目由劳埃德银行5K首付房贷赞助，这是自1996年以来再次出现的产品。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the 1990s looks now like a lost golden age of prosperity and positivity, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 没错，所以20世纪90年代现在看起来就像是一个繁荣与乐观的失落黄金时代，不是吗？

sentences.en: Think of the sort of the advent of the Blair administration in 1997, all the enthusiasm and excitement that surrounded that,
sentences.zh: 想想1997年布莱尔政府上台时，周围那种满腔的热情与兴奋，

sentences.en: the economic growth of the time, the technological developments, the sort of sense of an endless golden summer
sentences.zh: 当时的经济增长、技术发展，以及那种仿佛无休止的黄金夏日感，

sentences.en: where everybody's listening to Blair and Oasis and looking forward to buying their first houses.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在听布莱尔和绿洲乐队的歌，并期待着买下他们的第一套房子。

sentences.en: And that, of course, takes us to mortgages.
sentences.zh: 而这，自然就让我们想到了房贷。

sentences.en: Now, the good news is that in a nod to the 1990s, Lloyd's are offering 5K deposit mortgages to first-time buyers.
sentences.zh: 好消息是，为了向20世纪90年代致敬，劳埃德银行正向首次购房者提供5K首付的房贷。

sentences.en: So search 5K first-time buyer.
sentences.zh: 所以请搜索“5K首次购房者”。

sentences.en: 1996 average first-time buyer deposits are based on ONS data.
sentences.zh: 1996年首次购房者的平均首付数据基于英国国家统计局（ONS）。

sentences.en: Subject to status, your home may be repossessed if you don't keep up repayments, and conditions apply.
sentences.zh: 视信用状况而定，如果未能按时还款，您的房屋可能会被收回，并适用相关条款。

sentences.en: An old servant was waiting for us by a small iron door.
sentences.zh: 一个老仆人在一扇小铁门旁等候着我们。

sentences.en: He led us through a number of dark stairs and rooms, until he asked us to enter a certain door.
sentences.zh: 他带着我们走过许多昏暗的楼梯和房间，直到请我们走进某扇门。

sentences.en: As I crossed the threshold, a black bird, some kind of raven, flew at my head.
sentences.zh: 当我跨过门槛时，一只黑色的鸟，某种乌鸦，朝我的头扑了过来。

sentences.en: A voice called from the next room.
sentences.zh: 隔壁房间传出一个声音。

sentences.en: Please come in.
sentences.zh: 请进。

sentences.en: Marie ushered me in.
sentences.zh: 玛丽把我迎了进去。

sentences.en: We talked a while about Vienna.
sentences.zh: 我们聊了一会儿关于维也纳的事。

sentences.en: Then he said to me,
sentences.zh: 然后他对我说，

sentences.en: Pardon me, but I would like to talk to the countess privately for a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 请原谅，但我想和伯爵夫人单独谈几分钟。

sentences.en: Then he went with Marie to another room.
sentences.zh: 接着他和玛丽去了另一个房间。

sentences.en: I looked around me.
sentences.zh: 我环顾四周。

sentences.en: On his desk was a revolver and a skull.
sentences.zh: 他的书桌上放着一把左轮手枪和一个头骨。

sentences.en: I picked up the skull, took it between my hands, and looked at it from all sides.
sentences.zh: 我拿起头骨，把它拿在手中，从各个角度端详着它。

sentences.en: Suddenly, Rodolf came in and took it from me with deep apprehension.
sentences.zh: 突然，鲁道夫走了进来，满怀忧虑地把它从我手中拿了过去。

sentences.en: But when I said that I wasn't afraid, he smiled.
sentences.zh: 但当我笑着说我不害怕时，他笑了。

sentences.en: So that is an amazing scene, like something, and we said it before, from a kind of gothic melodrama, Edgar Allan Poe, or something like that.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个令人惊叹的场景，就像我们之前说过的那样，带有某种哥特式情节剧的风格，比如埃德加·爱伦·坡或类似的作品。

sentences.en: But in fact, that is a letter that was written by the 17-year-old Baroness Mary Vetsera to her old governess in the autumn of 1888.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，这是一封由17岁的玛丽·韦策拉男爵小姐在1888年秋天写给她老家庭教师的信。

sentences.en: In fact, it's like something out of Dracula, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 事实上，这感觉就像《德古拉》里的情节，不是吗？

sentences.en: A letter written to a governess by a 17-year-old girl who has invited herself into the room of an exceedingly sinister man.
sentences.zh: 这是一封由一个17岁女孩写给家庭教师的信，她不请自来地闯入了一个极其阴险的男人的房间。

sentences.en: And she is describing there a secret meeting with the heir to the throne of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, Crown Prince Rudolf.
sentences.zh: 她在信中描述了与奥匈帝国皇位继承人鲁道夫皇储的一次秘密会面。

sentences.en: And this had happened a few days earlier on the 5th of November.
sentences.zh: 而这发生在几天前的11月5日。

sentences.en: And Dominic, if listeners, which I hope they will have done, have heard our first episode, then they will know where this is heading.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，如果听众们听过了我们的第一集——我希望他们已经听过了——那么他们就会知道这件事将走向何方。

sentences.en: And it is nowhere good for Baroness Mary, because she is heading to a hunting lodge at Meiling in the Vienna woods.
sentences.zh: 这对玛丽男爵小姐来说绝对不是什么好事，因为她正前往维也纳森林中梅林的一个狩猎小屋。

sentences.en: And what happens there is going to be one of the greatest scandals in the entire history, not just of Austro-Hungarian, but of European royalty.
sentences.zh: 在那里发生的事情将成为整个皇室历史上最大的丑闻之一，不仅是奥匈帝国，乃至整个欧洲皇室。

sentences.en: It is going to be a murder-suicide pact that will shake the Habsburg dynasty to its very foundations.
sentences.zh: 这将是一场谋杀与自杀的协议，它将动摇哈布斯堡王朝的根基。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, it's an amazing story.
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，这是一个惊人的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is an amazing, amazing tale.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个极其惊人的故事。

sentences.en: And today we'll be telling the story of that secret affair between Rudolf and Mary.
sentences.zh: 今天我们将讲述鲁道夫和玛丽之间那段秘密恋情的故事。

sentences.en: We will get deep into what exactly happened at Meiling, and we'll talk about the implications for the Habsburg dynasty and for the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
sentences.zh: 我们将深入探讨梅林到底发生了什么，并讨论其对哈布斯堡王朝和奥匈帝国的深远影响。

sentences.en: But just to remind ourselves exactly when and where we are, we're in Vienna in 1888, the world of Klimt and Freud and Mahler and these titanic cultural figures.
sentences.zh: 但为了提醒我们自己到底身处何时何地，我们正处于1888年的维也纳，这是一个属于克里姆特、弗洛伊德、马勒以及这些文化巨匠的世界。

sentences.en: Also the world of Crown Prince Rudolf, the sinister man in the Gothic melodrama that you described so chillingly, I have to say, in your introductory reading.
sentences.zh: 这也是皇储鲁道夫的世界，也就是你在开场导读中以极其令人不寒而栗的方式所描述的那部哥特式情节剧中的阴险男人。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So, Crown Prince Rudolf is 30 years old.
sentences.zh: 所以，皇储鲁道夫当时30岁。

sentences.en: He is, to remind people, he is the son of Emperor Franz Joseph and his very glamorous, kind of melancholy wife, Cece.
sentences.zh: 提醒大家一下，他是弗兰茨·约瑟夫皇帝与他那位光彩照人、带有一点忧郁气质的妻子茜茜的儿子。

sentences.en: Very thin, very long hair.
sentences.zh: 非常瘦，头发非常长。

sentences.en: And Rudolf, who takes after his mother, I think it's reasonable to surmise.
sentences.zh: 我认为合理推测，鲁道夫很像他的母亲。

sentences.en: He is a very troubled, unhappy, kind of morbid young man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个饱受困扰、极不快乐、带有某种病态的年轻男子。

sentences.en: He's almost certainly suffering from incurable gonorrhea.
sentences.zh: 他几乎可以肯定是患有无法治愈的淋病。

sentences.en: He's probably off his face on morphine, and he is suffocated by the kind of expectations of his role as Crown Prince.
sentences.zh: 他可能吸毒过量神志不清，并且被皇储这个身份的种种期望压得喘不过气来。

sentences.en: And also, I think he is being eaten away by a sense of uselessness and futility as he waits for his father to die and to vacate the throne.
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为他在等待父亲去世并腾出王位的同时，也被一种无用感和徒劳感一点点吞噬着。

sentences.en: And into Rudolf's orbit, as we described last time, has come the teenage Baroness Mary Vetsera.
sentences.zh: 正如我们上次所说，十几岁的玛丽·韦策拉男爵小姐闯入了鲁道夫的生命轨道。

sentences.en: She is precocious, she's a social butterfly, she's a social climber, she's ambitious, but she's also incredibly romantic in a very 17-year-old, sort of teenage girl way.
sentences.zh: 她早熟，是个交际花，是个想往上爬的人，很有野心，但同时她也带着一种极其符合17岁少女特质的浪漫情怀。

sentences.en: Well, you could see, couldn't you, from that extract that she wrote, is it actually like a gothic melodrama, or is she putting that spin on it?
sentences.zh: 好吧，从她写的那个片段里你也能看出来，不是吗？这究竟真的像是一部哥特式情节剧，还是她自己给它加上了这种滤镜？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然是。

sentences.en: Bit of both, probably.
sentences.zh: 可能两方面都有吧。

sentences.en: Was there really a blackbird, you know?
sentences.zh: 真的有一只乌鸦吗，你知道的？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it's improbable.
sentences.zh: 对啊，我的意思是，这不太可能。

sentences.en: And she had gone to that meeting with her older friend, Countess Marie Larish, who is Rudolf's cousin.
sentences.zh: 而且她是和她较大的朋友、鲁道夫的表妹玛丽·拉里什伯爵夫人一起去赴约的。

sentences.en: And basically, the Countess, Larish, has acted as the sort of intermediary and put the two of them together.
sentences.zh: 基本上，拉里什伯爵夫人充当了某种中间人的角色，把他们两个人撮合在了一起。

sentences.en: The board.
sentences.zh: 这个局中人。

sentences.en: She is the board, yeah.
sentences.zh: 她就是那个局，对。

sentences.en: You could say she's the procurer, as it were.
sentences.zh: 你可以说她是个拉皮条的，算是吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, the events that you described, Monday the 5th of November, 1888, we ended the last episode with this scene.
sentences.zh: 所以，你描述的那些事件发生于1888年11月5日星期一，上一集的结尾我们定格在了这个场景。

sentences.en: Countess Larish has offered to take Mary shopping with her mother's permission.
sentences.zh: 拉里什伯爵夫人提出在得到玛丽母亲允许的情况下带玛丽去购物。

sentences.en: They went to the Graben, the Great Shopping Street in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 他们去了维也纳的大购物街格拉本大街。

sentences.en: They went to a society photographer to have Mary's picture taken, but then they went to the back entrance to the Grand Hotel, to a carriage, which was waiting for them,
sentences.zh: 他们去了一家社交摄影师那里给玛丽拍照，但随后他们去了大酒店的后门，上了一辆马车，马车一直在等他们，

sentences.en: driven by Rudolf's coachman, Josef Bratfish.
sentences.zh: 车夫是鲁道夫的御者约瑟夫·布拉特菲施。

sentences.en: Bratfish?
sentences.zh: 布拉特菲施？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a great name.
sentences.zh: 对，这名字真棒。

sentences.en: That is worthy of an American.
sentences.zh: 这名字配得上一个美国人。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全赞同。

sentences.en: It is, yeah.
sentences.zh: 确实，对。

sentences.en: And Dominic, this whole thing about women being taken to the, you know, to hotels, the back rooms of hotels and things, and being driven off in carriages.
sentences.zh: 而且多米尼克，整件事关于女性被带到酒店，你知道的，酒店的后房之类的地方，然后坐马车被载走。

sentences.en: Faint echo of Diana about this, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 这让人隐约联想到戴安娜，不是吗？

sentences.en: We kind of mentioned it in the context of Sisi.
sentences.zh: 我们在茜茜的语境下顺带提过这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely there is.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对有。

sentences.en: I mean, it's very much a kind of Diana in the 1990s vibe to this, I think.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得这非常有一种20世纪90年代戴安娜的风范。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Diana's story doesn't quite have that gothic element to it, though, does it?
sentences.zh: 不过戴安娜的故事并没有那种哥特式元素，对吧？

sentences.en: It's rather more Hello Magazine.
sentences.zh: 它更像是《你好》杂志的风格。

sentences.en: This is much more Hello Magazine meets Bram Stoker, as you said.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这更像是《你好》杂志遇上了布拉姆·斯托克。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So from there, she was taken to the Hofburg, the Imperial Palace, to Rudolf's private apartments, and then we get the scene with the raven and the skull.
sentences.zh: 所以从那里，她被带到了霍夫堡宫，即皇宫，来到了鲁道夫的私人公寓，然后就上演了乌鸦和头骨的那一幕。

sentences.en: And so begins their relationship, their affair.
sentences.zh: 他们的关系、他们的恋情就这样开始了。

sentences.en: Now, this is not unusual for Rudolf.
sentences.zh: 好了，这对于鲁道夫来说并不罕见。

sentences.en: Rudolf has had a lot of affairs.
sentences.zh: 鲁道夫有过很多风流韵事。

sentences.en: And all the time, he's still seeing his chief, his regular mistress, who is the former courtesan, Mitzi Kaspar.
sentences.zh: 而且在此期间，他仍然在和他的情人、常规情妇——前名妓米齐·卡斯帕见面。

sentences.en: And Mary herself, actually, this is not her first rodeo.
sentences.zh: 其实玛丽自己也不是第一次经历这种事了。

sentences.en: So she, for an aristocratic girl of 17, is probably quite experienced.
sentences.zh: 所以对于一个17岁的贵族女孩来说，她可能相当有经验。

sentences.en: She'd been on a trip to Egypt a year earlier, and it was generally thought that she'd been carrying on with a British brigadier.
sentences.zh: 她一年前曾去埃及旅行过，人们普遍认为她当时和一个英国准将有染。

sentences.en: Oh, my goodness.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Not General Gordon.
sentences.zh: 不是戈登将军吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That would be improbable.
sentences.zh: 那可太不可思议了。

sentences.en: Wow, that's a twiSt.
sentences.zh: 哇，真是个反转。

sentences.en: General Gordon, who is still alive in this version of history.
sentences.zh: 戈登将军在这版历史里居然还活着。

sentences.en: Okay, fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧，行吧。

sentences.en: Well, anyway, she's had loads of admirers, not just Crown Prince Rudolf.
sentences.zh: 总之，她有过无数追求者，不只是鲁道夫皇储。

sentences.en: So what makes this particular liaison so special?
sentences.zh: 那么是什么让这段特定的恋情如此特殊呢？

sentences.en: Well, you described how Mary Vetsera's account owes something to gothic melodrama.
sentences.zh: 你描述了玛丽·韦策拉的自述带有哥特式情节剧的色彩。

sentences.en: But it pales by comparison with this, which is from Rudolf's military aide, Victor von Frischer.
sentences.zh: 但与这个故事相比，它就显得黯然失色了，这是鲁道夫的军事副官维克托·冯·弗里舍讲述的。

sentences.en: And he tells this absolutely extraordinary story.
sentences.zh: 他讲了这个绝对非同寻常的故事。

sentences.en: He said later, you know, when we were young men, we were stationed in Prague when we were younger.
sentences.zh: 他后来讲过，你知道的，当年我们年轻的时候，年轻时曾被派驻到布拉格。

sentences.en: And we once went, me and Crown Prince Rudolf, to the ghetto cemetery.
sentences.zh: 有一次我和鲁道夫皇储一起去了犹太人隔离区的墓地。

sentences.en: You know the old town cemetery in Prague?
sentences.zh: 你知道布拉格那个老城墓地吗？

sentences.en: Very evocative, moving.
sentences.zh: 非常具有感染力，感人至深。

sentences.en: With the grave of the rabbi who created the golem.
sentences.zh: 里面有创造了泥人的那位拉比的墓。

sentences.en: The golem, exactly.
sentences.zh: 就是泥人，没错。

sentences.en: The kind of prototype for Frankenstein.
sentences.zh: 弗兰肯斯坦的原型。

sentences.en: So this really kind of haunting, spooky kind of landscape.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常令人难忘、带点诡异色彩的景观。

sentences.en: And they went there and the cantor was singing prayers during a funeral.
sentences.zh: 他们去的那天，领唱正是在葬礼上唱着祷告歌。

sentences.en: And Rudolf was very taken by this, according to his aide, and particularly by the cantor's raven-haired daughter.
sentences.zh: 根据他副官的说法，鲁道夫对此非常着迷，尤其是对领唱那个黑发女儿。

sentences.en: And she became obsessed with Crown Prince Rudolf too, so obsessed that her father had to send her to a provincial town to get her away from him.
sentences.zh: 她也对鲁道夫皇储迷恋至极，甚至到了她父亲不得不把她送到一个外省小镇以让她远离他的地步。

sentences.en: But she came back to Prague.
sentences.zh: 但她又回到了布拉格。

sentences.en: She stood every night under his castle window through the winter.
sentences.zh: 整个冬天，她每天夜里都站在他的城堡窗户下面。

sentences.en: Rudolf eventually found out that she was standing underneath his window.
sentences.zh: 鲁道夫最终发现她正站在自己的窗户底下。

sentences.en: But when he sent people to look for her, they reported that she had just caught pneumonia and died.
sentences.zh: 但当他派人去找她时，回报说她刚刚染上肺炎死去了。

sentences.en: And Rudolf went secretly to her grave and left roses by her tombstone.
sentences.zh: 鲁道夫秘密去了她的墓地，在她的墓碑旁留下玫瑰。

sentences.en: So do you think there's a possibility that that raven was the reincarnation of this girl who died of...
sentences.zh: 所以你觉得有没有可能，那只乌鸦就是这个因……而死的女孩的转世？

sentences.en: And I imagine it wasn't pneumonia, I imagine it was consumption.
sentences.zh: 而且我猜那不是肺炎，我猜那是肺结核。

sentences.en: Well, I think Viktor von Fritsch has a very lively imagination.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得维克托·冯·弗里舍有着非常丰富的想象力。

sentences.en: Because Viktor von Fritsch, Rudolf's aide, said, the Crown Prince clearly believed that this Mary Vetsera was the reincarnation of this Jewish girl from Prague.
sentences.zh: 因为鲁道夫的副官维克托·冯·弗里舍说过，皇储显然坚信这个玛丽·韦策拉就是那个布拉格犹太女孩的转世。

sentences.en: Oh God, there is reincarnation!
sentences.zh: 哦天哪，还真有转世这回事！

sentences.en: And this is why he was so obsessed with her.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他对她如此着迷。

sentences.en: This is his interpretation.
sentences.zh: 这是他的解读。

sentences.en: Whether listeners believe this, I'll leave to them.
sentences.zh: 至于听众们是否相信这一点，我就留给他们自己判断了。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't think she probably...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得她大概不可能是……

sentences.en: I don't think she was the reincarnation of this girl, but who knows?
sentences.zh: 我不认为她是那个女孩的转世，但谁知道呢？

sentences.en: But I suppose the question is whether Rudolf might have thought that.
sentences.zh: 不过我想问题在于鲁道夫当时是否可能是这么想的。

sentences.en: He might have done.
sentences.zh: 他很有可能是这么想的。

sentences.en: They get to Baden
sentences.zh: 他们到了巴登

sentences.zh: 车站，他不得不走进站长办公室说，皇太子

sentences.zh: 鲁道夫的猎村发生了一件可怕的事。

sentences.en: I must get to Vienna instantly.
sentences.zh: 我必须立刻去维也纳。

sentences.en: And the station master agrees to stop the express train from Trieste and Hoyos climbs on board.
sentences.zh: 站长同意拦截一列从里雅斯特开来的特快列车，霍约斯登上了火车。

sentences.zh: 所以在9点50分，他已经到了维也纳。

sentences.zh: 在大约25分钟内，他抵达了霍夫堡皇宫。

sentences.zh: 在这里，他彻底崩溃了。

sentences.en: He doesn't know how he can possibly break this news to the emperor.
sentences.zh: 他不知道该怎么向皇帝开口禀报这个消息。

sentences.en: So he goes to find
sentences.zh: 于是他去找

sentences.zh: 茜茜的内侍，名叫诺普萨男爵。

sentences.en: And they say, well, we will tell the empress and then she can tell the emperor.
sentences.zh: 他们商量说，好吧，我们先告诉皇后，然后由她去告诉皇帝。

sentences.en: So Cece, Elizabeth, she got up early that morning.
sentences.zh: 所以茜茜，也就是伊丽莎白，那天早上起得很早。

sentences.en: She got up at 6.30, as she always did.
sentences.zh: 她像往常一样，在6点30分就起床了。

sentences.en: Her days always began with this long bath and then a massage.
sentences.zh: 她的一天总是从长时间的泡澡开始，接着是按摩。

sentences.en: Then her hair, famously long.
sentences.zh: 然后是她标志性的一头长发。

sentences.en: There was a special maid to comb her hair.
sentences.zh: 有专门的宫女为她梳头。

sentences.en: Yeah, for two or three hours, learning Greek, all of that.
sentences.zh: 对，还要花两三个小时学习希腊语之类的。

sentences.en: Then she would have a herbal tea and she would do some exercises in her private gym.
sentences.zh: 然后她会喝一杯草本茶，并在私人健身房做一些运动。

sentences.en: Then she, at 10 o'clock, had started a Greek lesson with Monsieur Roussophilos.
sentences.zh: 接着，在10点钟，她开始跟鲁索菲洛斯先生上希腊语课。

sentences.en: And they were reading the Iliad together.
sentences.zh: 他们一起阅读《伊利亚特》。

sentences.en: And at 10.45, there was a knock on the door.
sentences.zh: 10点45分的时候，门被敲响了。

sentences.en: And the lady-in-waiting said, Baron Nopšča and Count Hoyos want to see you urgently.
sentences.zh: 女官说，诺普萨男爵和霍约斯伯爵有急事要见您。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth was furious.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白勃然大怒。

sentences.en: You don't interfere with my Greek lessons.
sentences.zh: 任何人都不准打扰我的希腊语课。

sentences.en: But then Baron Nopšča came in.
sentences.zh: 但接着诺普萨男爵走了进来。

sentences.en: She saw the look on his face and she realised something was terribly wrong.
sentences.zh: 她看到他脸上的神情，意识到出了大事。

sentences.en: Now, her husband, Franz Joseph, had been up even longer.
sentences.zh: 至于她的丈夫弗朗茨·约瑟夫，起得更早。

sentences.en: Well, he always gets up early, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他总是起得很早，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because he's got an empire to run.
sentences.zh: 因为他有一个庞大的帝国要管理。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He got up at four o'clock in the morning from his iron military bed.
sentences.zh: 他在清晨四点钟就从那张铁质行军床上醒来。

sentences.en: And he'd been washed by his footman.
sentences.zh: 他的贴身男仆帮他洗漱完毕。

sentences.en: He'd had breakfast at 4.20.
sentences.zh: 他在4点20分吃过早餐。

sentences.en: And then he got straight into his paperwork and had his first meetings at five o'clock in the morning.
sentences.zh: 然后他直接开始处理文书工作，并在早上五点钟召开了第一次会议。

sentences.en: And a lot of this had been about the Budapest parliament and the army bill.
sentences.zh: 其中大部分内容都与布达佩斯议会和陆军法案有关。

sentences.en: As Frederick Morton said, that morning,
sentences.zh: 正如弗雷德里克·莫顿所说，那天早晨，

sentences.en: Franz Joseph did what his ancestors had done before him.
sentences.zh: 弗朗茨·约瑟夫做着他的祖先们过去常做的事。

sentences.en: He ruled and overruled with utter confidence, with axiomatic competence, and without the slightest inspiration.
sentences.zh: 他以绝对的自信、不证自明的能力，以及毫无灵感的方式进行统治和独断。

sentences.en: Just before 11 o'clock, he set off to go to see his wife in her apartment.
sentences.zh: 就在11点之前，他动身前往他妻子的寝宫探望她。

sentences.en: Franz Joseph was looking forward to this because he knew that his wife actually had a pre-arranged meeting with his confidant, Katharina Schrat, the actress.
sentences.zh: 弗朗茨·约瑟夫对此充满期待，因为他知道妻子其实已经和他的红颜知己、女演员卡塔琳娜·施拉特约好了见面。

sentences.en: Katharina Schrat was going to do a drama recital for his wife.
sentences.zh: 卡塔琳娜·施拉特将为他的妻子表演一出戏剧朗诵。

sentences.en: And this is brilliant for him because he'll see his two favourite people at once.
sentences.zh: 这对他是极好的消息，因为他可以同时见到他最喜欢的两个人。

sentences.en: And, you know, their little menage, he loves all that.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，他们这种特殊的小圈子，他最喜欢这一套了。

sentences.en: But he gets there and he finds Baron
sentences.zh: 但等他到了那里，却发现

sentences.en: Knopster blocking the door to his wife's apartment.
sentences.zh: 诺普萨男爵挡住了他妻子寝宫的门。

sentences.en: Baron Knopster's face is streaked with tears.
sentences.zh: 诺普萨男爵的脸上挂满了泪痕。

sentences.en: And through the door, Franz Joseph can hear his wife sobbing and sobbing.
sentences.zh: 透过房门，弗朗茨·约瑟夫能听到他的妻子在里面痛哭流涕。

sentences.en: So in the next few hours, the news that something terrible has happened races around the city.
sentences.zh: 所以在接下来的几个小时里，可怕的事发生的噩耗传遍了整个城市。

sentences.en: Crown Prince Rudolf's wife,
sentences.zh: 皇太子鲁道夫的妻子，

sentences.en: Stephanie, is having a singing lesson and that's interrupted and she is told.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬妮正在上声乐课，结果课程被打断，她得知了噩耗。

sentences.en: And soon after that, all the operas, the theatres, the cabarets, the music halls are told to cancel their evening programmes with no explanation.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，所有的歌剧院、剧院、歌舞表演厅和音乐厅都被下令取消晚上的演出，且不作任何解释。

sentences.en: And by mid-afternoon, there's a crowd outside the Hofburg.
sentences.zh: 到了下午中期，霍夫堡皇宫外聚集了一群人。

sentences.en: People know something has happened.
sentences.zh: 人们知道出事了。

sentences.en: There are people talking about Crown Prince Rudolf, but no one knows exactly what it is.
sentences.zh: 有人在谈论皇太子鲁道夫，但没有人确切知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: And it's actually not until the following morning that the news is confirmed.
sentences.zh: 直到第二天早上，这个消息才得到证实。

sentences.en: It's broken by the Wiener Tagblatt.
sentences.zh: 它是由《维也纳日报》爆出来的。

sentences.en: Our Crown Prince is dead, says this huge headline.
sentences.zh: 我们的皇太子死了，这个巨大的标题这样写着。

sentences.en: It's reproduced, there's an image of it, in Frederick Morton's book, A Nervous Splendor.
sentences.zh: 它被转载了，在弗雷德里克·莫顿的书《神经质的辉煌》中还有它的图片。

sentences.en: But what there aren't are, there are no details of how he died.
sentences.zh: 但上面没有任何关于他是如何死去的细节。

sentences.en: So the assumption that most people make is he has had a stroke or a heart attack, you know, a freak accident or something, who knows?
sentences.zh: 所以大多数人的猜测是，他中风了，或者心脏病发作了，你知道的，遭遇了什么离奇的事故之类的，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Throttled by the Kaiser.
sentences.zh: 被皇帝给掐死了。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全有可能。

sentences.en: He's died of apoplexy after the Kaiser has been rude about an Austrian army belt or something of that kind, surely.
sentences.zh: 他肯定是死于中风，就因为皇帝对奥地利陆军的某种腰带或者类似的东西发了脾气，绝对是的。

sentences.en: A bit of the obvious explanation, wouldn't it?
sentences.zh: 这算是一个显而易见的解释，对吧？

sentences.en: But not, it's the following evening, the Wiener Tagblatt prints the headline,
sentences.zh: 然而并没有，直到第二天晚上，《维也纳日报》才刊登了这样的大标题：

sentences.en: The Most Horrible Truth.
sentences.zh: 《最可怕的真相》。

sentences.en: And it says, Crown Prince Rudolf was killed by a gunshot and he fired the pistol himself.
sentences.zh: 上面写着，皇太子鲁道夫死于枪伤，手枪是他自己开的。

sentences.en: I mean, I can't imagine, because it's still a very devoutly Catholic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，简直难以想象，因为这里依然是一个极其笃信天主教的

sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: City and country.
sentences.zh: 城市和国家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种冲击绝对是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: I mean, this is, we said it's the royal scandal, to end all royal scandals.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是我们所说的，足以终结一切皇室丑闻的终极皇室丑闻。

sentences.en: I mean, let's try to imagine, I mean, it's not even Prince Harry.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，让我们试着想象一下，这甚至不是哈里王子那种级别。

sentences.zh: 这简直就像是，难以置信地，你同为阿斯顿维拉球迷的同伴威廉王子。

sentences.en: Prince William.
sentences.zh: 威廉王子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 和一个17岁的女孩胡搞，然后在斯泰因斯的猎村搞出一个谋杀加自杀的协议。

sentences.en: I think it's much worse than that, because suicide is no longer framed as a sin.
sentences.zh: 我觉得情况远比这还要糟糕，因为现在自杀已经不再被视为一种罪过了。

sentences.en: No, it's true.
sentences.zh: 不，确实如此。

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 你知道的，现在人们会以同情和理解的眼光来看待它。

sentences.en: But back then, it was a sin.
sentences.zh: 但在当年，自杀可是一桩罪过。

sentences.en: I mean, it endangers your mortal soul.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这会危及你的灵魂不朽。

sentences.zh: 对于哈布斯堡家族来说，他们信奉天主教是其统治合法性的关键。

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.zh: 他们是天主教的守护者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们是绝对的，他的使徒陛下，弗朗茨·约瑟夫。

sentences.en: You know, it's so important for them as kings of Hungary and as emperors of Austria.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这对于身为匈牙利国王和奥地利皇帝的他们来说至关重要。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对如此。

sentences.en: So let's actually focus on the imperial family for a second.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们把焦点重新转回皇室家族身上片刻。

sentences.en: By the way, one small detail, actually, which I forgot to mention.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，其实还有一个小细节我刚才忘了提。

sentences.zh: 玛丽·韦策拉的名字在所有那些报纸报道中根本压根儿没被提及过。

sentences.zh: 我们一会儿再回过头来谈她在整个故事中的角色。

sentences.zh: 所以弗朗茨·约瑟夫在第一个下午的大部分时间里，都在卡塔琳娜·施拉特的陪同下试图安慰他的妻子。

sentences.en: And then being Franz Joseph, he went back to work.
sentences.zh: 然后，不愧是弗朗茨·约瑟夫，他又回去工作了。

sentences.en: And he worked late that night and he rang by 10 o'clock that night on the day he heard the news about his son.
sentences.zh: 那天夜里他工作到很晚，就在他听到儿子死讯的那天晚上十点钟左右，他还在打电话。

sentences.en: He was still ringing the Hungarian prime minister to talk about the army bill.
sentences.zh: 他当时还在给匈牙利首相打电话商讨陆军法案的事。

sentences.en: The next day, he got up at four o'clock as usual to start work.
sentences.zh: 第二天，他像往常一样在四点钟起床开始工作。

sentences.zh: 他也是第一个真正走进房间检查尸体的人。

sentences.zh: 威德霍弗教授说，我带来了一个非常糟糕的消息。

sentences.zh: 很显然，皇太子是自杀身亡的，头部中枪。

sentences.zh: 但更糟糕的是，毫无疑问，他在两小时前用同一把枪杀死了玛丽·韦策拉。

sentences.en: So actually, this is so interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，这真的太有意思了。

sentences.en: He had killed Mary Vetsera before he appeared at the manservant's bedside to say, get my breakfast ready.
sentences.zh: 他在出现在男仆床边说“帮我准备早餐”之前，就已经把玛丽·韦策拉给杀了。

sentences.en: To ask for breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 去要求吃早餐。

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 那么你觉得当时究竟发生什么了？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Did he ever plan to eat the breakfast?
sentences.zh: 他压根没打算吃早餐吗？

sentences.en: Change his mind?
sentences.zh: 改变主意了？

sentences.en: Impossible to say.
sentences.zh: 这很难说。

sentences.en: Strange.
sentences.zh: 真奇怪。

sentences.en: I mean, everything about this is strange.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这整件事都很奇怪。

sentences.zh: 这点我们无法否认。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 但我认为，对弗朗茨·约瑟夫来说，最糟糕的是维德霍弗接下来所说的话。

sentences.zh: 皇太子留下了好几封信。

sentences.en: So he's left a letter to his mother, Sisi.
sentences.zh: 所以他给母亲茜茜留了一封信。

sentences.en: This is the only letter that was written at the scene of the crime.
sentences.zh: 这是在犯罪现场写下的唯一一封信。

sentences.en: The other letters were written beforehand.
sentences.zh: 其他信件都是事先写好的。

sentences.zh: 他写信给母亲。

sentences.en: I have killed.

sentences.zh: 并且他请求将他和玛丽合葬在附近的海利根克鲁茨修道院。

sentences.en: Holy Cross.
sentences.zh: 圣十字修道院。

sentences.zh: 他事先给姐姐瓦莱丽写了一封信。

sentences.en: He said, I advise you.
sentences.zh: 他说，我劝你。

sentences.en: I'm going now.
sentences.zh: 我要走了。

sentences.en: I advise you when our father dies, leave Austria, for what will happen then in Austria is unforeseeable.
sentences.zh: 我劝你等父亲去世后离开奥地利，因为接下来在奥地利发生的事情将是不可预测的。

sentences.en: This is, again, his kind of existential apocalyptic dread about the geopolitical outlook for his country.
sentences.zh: 这再次体现了他那种对国家地缘政治前景的生存主义末日恐惧。

sentences.en: And a shrewd analysis.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个精明的分析。

sentences.en: Yeah, I guess so.
sentences.zh: 对，我想是的。

sentences.zh: 他写信给他的妻子斯蒂芬妮。

sentences.en: Dear Stephanie, you are now rid of my presence and annoyance.
sentences.zh: 亲爱的斯蒂芬妮，你现在摆脱了我的存在和烦扰。

sentences.en: Be happy in your own way.
sentences.zh: 用你自己的方式去寻找幸福吧。

sentences.en: Take care of the poor little one.
sentences.zh: 照顾好那个可怜的小家伙。

sentences.en: She is all that is left of me.
sentences.zh: 她是我留下的全部。

sentences.en: He wrote a letter to Lošček, his valet.
sentences.zh: 他给他的随从洛舍克写了一封信。

sentences.en: Thank you for all the years of service.
sentences.zh: 感谢你多年来的服务。

sentences.en: He also wrote letters to his friend, Baron Moritz Hirsch, and to his mistress, Mitzi Kaspar.
sentences.zh: 他还给他的朋友莫里茨·希尔施男爵和情妇米齐·卡斯帕写了信。

sentences.en: But the contents of those letters is unknown, has never been released.
sentences.zh: 但这些信件的内容不得而知，从未公开发表过。

sentences.en: And for his father, the emperor, there was no letter at all.
sentences.zh: 而对于他的父亲——皇帝，他根本没有留下一封信。

sentences.en: Nothing.
sentences.zh: 什么也没有。

sentences.en: Oh, dear.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.zh: 这就是医生对弗朗茨·约瑟夫说那番话的时刻。

sentences.en: That's the moment when Franz Josef loses his composure and he breaks down in tears and he collapses and falls to the ground.
sentences.zh: 那是弗朗茨·约瑟夫彻底失控、痛哭流涕并瘫倒在地的时刻。

sentences.en: And you can absolutely understand why.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以理解为什么会这样。

sentences.en: For a father, that would be...
sentences.zh: 对于一个父亲来说，那会是……

sentences.en: Of course, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，当然。

sentences.en: Devastating.
sentences.zh: 毁灭性的打击。

sentences.en: That would be almost the worst blow of all, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想，那几乎是最沉重的打击了。

sentences.en: Such kind of posthumous cruelty as well, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这也是一种死后的残酷，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So eventually he composes himself and he says, where is my son?
sentences.zh: 所以他最终平静下来，说道，我的儿子在哪儿？

sentences.en: And Dr. Wiedehofer said, well, we've brought the body back to the palace as you ordered.
sentences.zh: 维德霍弗医生说，嗯，我们已经按照您的吩咐把遗体运回宫殿了。

sentences.en: We've dressed him in uniform.
sentences.zh: 我们给他穿上了制服。

sentences.en: We've bandaged his head and we've put him in bed.
sentences.zh: 我们包扎了他的头部，把他安置在床上。

sentences.en: And Franz Josef went to his son's bedroom and he stood by his son's body for 15 minutes in silence.
sentences.zh: 弗朗茨·约瑟夫走到儿子的卧室，在儿子遗体旁默默站了15分钟。

sentences.en: Kind of vigil for a brother officer as per the army regulations.
sentences.zh: 按照军队条例，这有点像战友之间的守灵。

sentences.en: Always the way with him.
sentences.zh: 他一向如此。

sentences.en: And then he said to his aides, well, we have two priorities now.
sentences.zh: 然后他对他的随从说，好吧，我们现在有两项首要任务。

sentences.en: Number one, my son must have a Catholic burial.
sentences.zh: 第一，我的儿子必须按天主教仪式安葬。

sentences.en: The Habsburgs have Catholic burials, Catholic funerals, even though he is both a murderer and a suicide.
sentences.zh: 哈布斯堡家族的人都要举行天主教葬礼，尽管他既是杀人犯又是自杀者。

sentences.en: And then secondly, he said, all mention of this girl must be suppressed.
sentences.zh: 其次，他说，关于这个女孩的一切都必须封锁消息。

sentences.en: Her presence at the scene, her body, even her name must be deleted from the public record.
sentences.zh: 她在现场的存在、她的遗体，甚至她的名字都必须从公众记录中抹去。

sentences.en: Now, what made this difficult is that the Habsburgs themselves have told the Vetsera family what happened to Mary.
sentences.zh: 现在，让事情变得困难的是，哈布斯堡家族自己把发生的事情告诉了韦采拉家族。

sentences.en: Cece herself broke the news to Mary's mother.
sentences.zh: 茜茜亲自把这个消息告诉了玛丽的母亲。

sentences.en: Now, at the time, the imperial staff said to Mary's mother, Baroness Hélène Vetsera, they said, you have to get out of Vienna.
sentences.zh: 当时，宫廷官员对玛丽的母亲海伦·韦采拉男爵夫人说，你们必须离开维也纳。

sentences.en: You know, the press will be hounding you.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，记者会纠缠不休。

sentences.en: There'll be crowds baying for your blood.
sentences.zh: 会有大批人群对你恨之入骨。

sentences.en: People will blame your daughter for this and you have to get out.
sentences.zh: 人们会把这归咎于你的女儿，你必须离开。

sentences.en: And she got on a train to Italy.
sentences.zh: 于是她登上了去意大利的火车。

sentences.en: But then she changed her mind halfway and she came back to the city.
sentences.zh: 但中途她改变了主意，又回到了城里。

sentences.en: And she found that the city police had cordoned off her townhouse, her mansion, because there were crowds outside.
sentences.zh: 她发现市警察局已经封锁了她的城镇宅邸和府邸，因为外面聚集了大量人群。

sentences.en: She was in a terrible state.
sentences.zh: 她当时状态极糟。

sentences.en: She wanted to go into the house.
sentences.zh: 她想进屋去。

sentences.en: And eventually, the Austrian prime minister, Count Tarfer, turned up.
sentences.zh: 最终，奥地利首相陶夫费伯爵出现了。

sentences.en: He was very, I think we described in the last episode, he's a very suave, kind of top hat cigar.
sentences.zh: 他非常……我想我们在上一集里描述过，他非常温文尔雅，戴着高顶礼帽，叼着雪茄。

sentences.en: And he sort of said, my dear, my dear lady, what a terrible business this is for you.
sentences.zh: 他差不多是说，亲爱的，我亲爱的夫人，对您来说这真是件糟糕的事。

sentences.en: I really do think you should get out of the city and you should keep a very low profile.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为您应该离开这座城市，并且保持低调。

sentences.en: It's now clear, by the way, that this was a genuine suicide pact because Mary's mother is now given a letter by Mary.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，现在很清楚这确实是一场殉情协定，因为玛丽的母亲现在收到了玛丽留下的一封信。

sentences.en: Forgive me for what I've done.
sentences.zh: 请原谅我所做的事。

sentences.en: I could not resist love.
sentences.zh: 我无法抗拒爱情。

sentences.en: In agreement with him, I wish to be buried by his side at the Alland churchyard.
sentences.zh: 经与他协商，我希望被安葬在阿兰德墓园他身旁。

sentences.en: It's actually a slightly different place from the Heilig and Croix Abbey, but there you go.
sentences.zh: 这其实跟海利根克鲁茨修道院稍微有点不同，不过就是这样。

sentences.en: I'm happier in death than I was in life.
sentences.zh: 我在死后比活着时更快乐。

sentences.en: I mean, imagine what that must be like for a mother to read from her daughter.
sentences.zh: 我是说，想象一下母亲读到女儿写下这些话时的感受。

sentences.en: Of course, there is a big issue here for the families now.
sentences.zh: 当然，这里对家族来说有个大问题。

sentences.en: If Mary and Rudolf are suicides, they cannot be buried in consecrated ground.
sentences.zh: 如果玛丽和鲁道夫是自杀的，他们就不能埋葬在祝圣过的墓地里。

sentences.en: The emperor, however, gets in touch with Heilig and Croix Abbey and his staff do anyway.
sentences.zh: 然而，皇帝还是通过他的随从联系了海利根克鲁茨修道院。

sentences.en: And they say, basically, we want you to find room for Mary Vetsera's body.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上说，我们希望你们为玛丽·韦采拉的遗体腾出地方。

sentences.en: Mary, no questions asked.
sentences.zh: 玛丽，无需多问。

sentences.en: You must find her a plot.
sentences.zh: 你们必须给她找块墓地。

sentences.en: And that same day, Thursday, the 31st of January, two of her uncles, the Baltazzi brothers, went to Myerling.
sentences.zh: 就在同一天，1月31日星期四，她的两个舅舅巴尔塔齐兄弟去了迈耶林。

sentences.en: They identified her body.
sentences.zh: 他们辨认了她的遗体。

sentences.en: A doctor washed the blood off her body and they dressed it in coat and hat, in a sort of veil, a boa, shoes.
sentences.zh: 一个医生洗去了她身上的血迹，他们给她穿上了外套和帽子，戴上了某种面纱、羽毛围巾和鞋子。

sentences.en: You know, remember, she's very fashionable.
sentences.zh: 要知道，记住，她非常时髦。

sentences.en: And then an absolutely bizarre scene.
sentences.zh: 随后发生了极其离奇的一幕。

sentences.en: Mary's uncles propped her up and walked her out of the hunting lodge as if she was alive and put her in the carriage and sat either side of her.
sentences.zh: 玛丽的舅舅们把她撑起来，像她还活着一样扶着她走出狩猎小屋，把她扶上马车，坐在她两侧。

sentences.en: So if anybody's seen the film Weekend at Bernie's, that's what this is.
sentences.zh: 所以如果有人看过电影《老板度假记》（Weekend at Bernie's），这就是怎么回事了。

sentences.en: And they even stuck a broomstick up the back of her dress so that it would keep her upright.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至把一根扫帚柄插在她裙子背面，好让她保持直立。

sentences.en: Because there are all kinds of stories where Sherlock Holmes turns up.
sentences.zh: 因为流传着各种福尔摩斯现身的说法。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And solves the case, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 并且侦破了这个案件，不是吗？

sentences.en: I don't think he'd have been fooled by that.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他会被那招糊弄过去。

sentences.en: No, he wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 不，他不会的。

sentences.en: I mean, this is so Sherlock Holmes, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这太像福尔摩斯探案了，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's sort of scandal in Bohemia.
sentences.zh: 有点像《波希米亚丑闻》。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, all of that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So the carriage rolled through the night to Heiligenkreuz Abbey, which is about three miles away.
sentences.zh: 于是马车在夜色中驶向大约三英里外的海利根克鲁茨修道院。

sentences.en: There were loads of police waiting.
sentences.zh: 那里有大批警察在等候。

sentences.en: And only the next morning, when the rain stopped a little bit, they buried Mary.
sentences.zh: 直到第二天早上，雨稍微停了点，他们才埋葬了玛丽。

sentences.en: And then the police sent a coded telegram to Vienna just with the words, all finished.
sentences.zh: 随后警察向维也纳发了一封加密电报，里面只有几个字：全部结束。

sentences.en: And that was the end in every way of Mary Vetsera.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·韦采拉的一切就这样彻底画上了句号。

sentences.en: There was one mention of her in an illustrated paper published in Graz, which said, quite erroneously,
sentences.zh: 格拉茨出版的一份画报上曾对她有过一次提及，其中完全错误地写道：

sentences.en: Mary Vetsera died in Venice and has been buried in Bohemia.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·韦采拉在威尼斯去世，并已在波希米亚安葬。

sentences.en: But otherwise, to quote Frederick Morton, her name never appeared again in any book, magazine or newspaper published in Austria-Hungary.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，用弗雷德里克·莫顿的话来说，她的名字再也没有出现在奥匈帝国出版的任何书籍、杂志或报纸上。

sentences.en: No printed mention was ever made of her death or even her life.
sentences.zh: 没有任何印刷品提及她的死讯，甚至连她的人生都没有提过。

sentences.en: It was as though nobody remembered that she had walked the earth.
sentences.zh: 就好像没有人记得她曾在这世上走过一遭。

sentences.en: So that is a contrast with Diana in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 所以这与90年代的戴安娜形成了鲜明对比。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because nobody was going to leave the details of that alone.
sentences.zh: 因为没有人会放过那些细节不管。

sentences.en: And in fact, they came up with all kinds of linked conspiracies to explain it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们还想出了各种乱七八糟的阴谋论来解释这件事。

sentences.en: But I'm wondering, what about the foreign press?
sentences.zh: 但我在想，外国媒体呢？

sentences.en: Well, come on to that in just a sec, but you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们马上就会谈到这点，不过你完全说得对。

sentences.en: Of course, the foreign press does print it.
sentences.zh: 当然，外国媒体确实报道了。

sentences.en: And a problem for the Austro-Hungarian monarchy is there's an extremely large country to their north that prints everything in German so people can read it.
sentences.zh: 奥匈帝国君主国面临的一个问题是，在他们北部有一个极其庞大的国家，那里用德语出版一切内容，因此人们都能看懂。

sentences.en: And it's very easy for people to travel between Germany and Austria-Hungary with German newspapers.
sentences.zh: 人们带着德国报纸在德国和奥匈帝国之间旅行非常方便。

sentences.en: So they're fooling nobody.
sentences.zh: 所以他们谁也骗不了。

sentences.en: I mean, people, everybody knows about it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，人们，每个人都知道这件事。

sentences.en: You know, they don't fool anybody.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们谁也糊弄不了。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, what about Crown Prince Rudolf?
sentences.zh: 与此同时，皇太子鲁道夫呢？

sentences.en: Well, they held an autopsy the same day, the 31St.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们在同一天——31日进行了尸检。

sentences.en: And the autopsy concluded that on studying Rudolf's brain, it was clear he was suffering from abnormal mental conditions and was in a state of mental confusion.
sentences.zh: 尸检结论显示，在研究了鲁道夫的大脑后，很明显他患有精神异常，并处于精神错乱的状态。

sentences.en: And the Catholic Church said, oh, well, in that case, you know, he's not really a suicide, is he?
sentences.zh: 天主教会说，哦，好吧，既然如此，你知道的，他其实不算自杀，对吧？

sentences.en: Or even a murderer.
sentences.zh: 甚至不算谋杀。

sentences.en: He was a poor fellow.
sentences.zh: 他是个可怜人。

sentences.en: What a terrible shame.
sentences.zh: 真是太遗憾了。

sentences.en: He can be buried on the Capuchin Crypt in Vienna alongside his ancestors.
sentences.zh: 他可以被安葬在维也纳的嘉布遣会地下墓穴，同他的祖先们合葬在一起。

sentences.en: And this apparently was quite common.
sentences.zh: 显然，这在当时相当常见。

sentences.en: Vienna, you know, coroners or whatever, were well known for fudging reports on suicides to allow people to be buried according to the rights of the church.
sentences.zh: 维也纳的验尸官之类的人，篡改自杀报告以允许死者按照教会仪式安葬是出了名的。

sentences.en: I think, though, it's very unusual for a case that is this high profile.
sentences.zh: 不过我认为，对于一个备受瞩目的案件来说，这非常罕见。

sentences.en: So the papal nuncio in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 所以驻维也纳的教皇使节。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And he says it's probably the first time that a papal nuncio had ever been obliged to attend the funeral of a murderer and a suicide.
sentences.zh: 他说这可能是教皇使节第一次被迫出席一个杀人犯兼自杀者的葬礼。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: So he's not happy about it at all.
sentences.zh: 所以他对此一点也不高兴。

sentences.en: And the papal nuncio actually then went to the hunting lodge and asked a load of questions, kept kind of looking into it.
sentences.zh: 然后教皇使节亲自去了那座狩猎小屋，问了一堆问题，一直在深入调查。

sentences.en: So he could team up with Bratfish.
sentences.zh: 这样他就可以和布拉特菲什组队了。

sentences.en: Set up an agency if the papal nuncioing doesn't work out.
sentences.zh: 如果当教皇使节混不下去了就去开个事务所。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太绝了。

sentences.en: So anyway, Rudolf lies in state for three days, various places in the Hofburg.
sentences.zh: 总之，鲁道夫的遗体在霍夫堡宫的各个地方停灵三天。

sentences.en: And finally, in the Hofburg Chapel, the Hofburg Capella.
sentences.zh: 最后在霍夫堡宫礼拜堂，即霍夫堡小教堂。

sentences.en: And there was a huge public crush, all thousands upon thousands of people, especially women, dressed in black.
sentences.zh: 当时有大批民众拥挤不堪，成千上万的人，尤其是穿着黑衣的女性。

sentences.en: So many that people were injured or fainted in the crowd.
sentences.zh: 人多到人群中有人受伤或晕倒。

sentences.en: Ambulances had to be called.
sentences.zh: 不得不叫了救护车。

sentences.en: And it ended with thousands of people being turned away.
sentences.zh: 结果有数以千计的人被拒之门外。

sentences.en: And then the funeral took place on Tuesday, the 5th of February in the Capuchin Church in the Capuchin Crypt, which you can visit.
sentences.zh: 然后葬礼于2月5日星期二在卡普钦教堂的卡普钦皇家墓穴举行，那个地方大家是可以去参观的。

sentences.en: I mean, you can see Crown Prince Rudolf's tomb.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你可以看到皇储鲁道夫的陵墓。

sentences.en: I went to see it last summer.
sentences.zh: 我去年夏天去看过。

sentences.en: Of course, this is not the last, you know, very high profile funeral there's going to be in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并不是维也纳将要迎来的最后一场，你知道的，备受瞩目的葬礼。

sentences.en: And not for the last time.
sentences.zh: 也绝不是最后一次。

sentences.en: Franz Josef specifically asks foreign dignitaries not to come.
sentences.zh: 弗朗茨·约瑟夫特意要求外国政要不要出席。

sentences.en: And in a preview of what will happen in 1914, the worst person, the last person you would ever want at a somber family occasion, the Kaiser, says, no, no, I'm coming anyway.
sentences.zh: 而作为1914年事件的预演，那个最糟糕的人——也就是你最不希望出现在肃穆家庭场合的最后一个人——德皇，却说，不，不，我无论如何都要来。

sentences.en: And Franz Josef has to send him a special message.
sentences.zh: 结果弗朗茨·约瑟夫不得不给他发了一封特殊的电报。

sentences.en: You may judge how deeply crushed my family is if we have to address this request, even to you, even to you, even to you.
sentences.zh: 如果我们要把这个请求向你提出，甚至向你提出，甚至向你提出，你就可以想象我的家族是多么的心碎。

sentences.en: If you'd suffered a terrible tragedy.
sentences.zh: 如果你曾遭受过可怕的悲剧。

sentences.en: And then Kaiser Wilhelm II announced that he was going to turn up.
sentences.zh: 然后德皇威廉二世宣布他要出席。

sentences.en: I mean, that would be the that would be the worSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那将会是——那将会是糟糕透顶的。

sentences.en: So the funeral was another incredibly sort of Viennese occasion.
sentences.zh: 所以这场葬礼又是那种极具维也纳特色的大场面。

sentences.en: The ritual would be that the chamberlain would knock on the door of the Capuchin Crypt and the voice would say, who is it?
sentences.zh: 当时的仪式是，宫廷侍臣会敲响卡普钦皇家墓穴的门，然后里面会传出一个声音问：是谁？

sentences.en: And he'd say, his most serene imperial and royal highness, the Archduke crown Prince Rudolf of Habsburg.
sentences.zh: 他会回答：至尊至贵的奥地利大公兼皇储、哈布斯堡的鲁道夫殿下。

sentences.en: And the voice would say, we know him not.
sentences.zh: 接着那个声音会说：我们不认识他。

sentences.en: And they'd repeat this.
sentences.zh: 他们会重复这个过程。

sentences.en: And then eventually, when the voice said, who is there?
sentences.zh: 最后，当那个声音问：外面是谁？

sentences.en: The chamberlain would say, your brother Rudolf, a poor sinner.
sentences.zh: 侍臣会说：你的兄弟鲁道夫，一个可怜的罪人。

sentences.en: And then at last, they would open the door and let him in.
sentences.zh: 然后他们最终才会打开门让他进去。

sentences.en: And then right at the end, very memorable moment when they carried the body down to the crypt.
sentences.zh: 而在最后，有一个非常难忘的时刻，当他们将遗体抬进墓穴时。

sentences.en: Franz Josef, the emperor.
sentences.zh: 皇帝弗朗茨·约瑟夫。

sentences.en: That's the one moment in public.
sentences.zh: 那是他在公众面前的唯一一次。

sentences.en: One of the only moments in his entire life.
sentences.zh: 他一生中仅有的几次时刻之一。

sentences.en: Probably the only moment when he lost control of his public dignity and he burst out crying and he broke down and he was kissing the casket and sobbing.
sentences.zh: 很可能是唯一一次他失去了公众尊严的控制，放声大哭，情绪崩溃，亲吻着棺木并啜泣。

sentences.en: The one moment when you see the man, you know, the grieving father behind the facade of the sort of the imperial walrus.
sentences.zh: 这是唯一一次让你看到这个男人，你知道的，在帝国海象胡须般的威严外表背后的那个悲伤的父亲。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So if we widen the picture out a bit, at one level, it's only a royal scandal.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们把视野稍微放宽一点，从某种层面来看，这只是一场皇室丑闻。

sentences.en: But the great sort of Austrian music critic, the most forbidding critic in Vienna of the day, was a guy called Edouard Hanslick.
sentences.zh: 但当时的维也纳有一位伟大的奥地利音乐评论家，也是当时维也纳最令人敬畏的评论家，他叫埃杜瓦尔德·汉斯利克。

sentences.en: And he wrote afterwards, he said, I've lived through the saddest catastrophes in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 他事后写道，他说，我经历过维也纳最悲伤的灾难。

sentences.en: I've lived through revolutions, the loss of land, murderous devastations by flood and fire.
sentences.zh: 我经历过革命、土地丧失、以及水火带来的毁灭性破坏。

sentences.en: But nothing of all this is comparable to the horror of January the 30th.
sentences.zh: 但所有这一切都无法与1月30日的恐怖相提并论。

sentences.en: The disconsolate, desperate turbulence which ripped through the entire population is indescribable.
sentences.zh: 那场撕裂了整个底层民众的悲痛欲绝、绝望混乱的场面是无法用言语形容的。

sentences.en: And we know from, I mean, you mentioned Diana a few times,
sentences.zh: 而且我们知道，我的意思是，你多次提到了戴安娜，

sentences.en: how these sort of personal tragedies can often cut through with the great mass of the population in a way that geopolitical things don't.
sentences.zh: 这类个人悲剧往往能以地缘政治事件所无法做到的方式，深深触动广大民众。

sentences.en: I mean, you said that Diana's world wasn't gothic, it was Hello magazine and everything.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你曾说过戴安娜的世界不是哥特式的，而是《你好》杂志那种风格以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And so it seemed expressive of a kind of age of celebrity that was running out of control.
sentences.zh: 所以它似乎体现了一种走向失控的名人文化时代。

sentences.en: But presumably in the Viennese context, there are all kinds of cultural swirls that find echoes in this case.
sentences.zh: 但想必在维也纳的语境下，各种文化思潮都在这个案件中找到了回响。

sentences.en: And also there is the sense that the crown prince is gone.
sentences.zh: 而且人们也会有一种感觉，那就是皇储不在了。

sentences.en: The emperor doesn't have another direct male heir.
sentences.zh: 皇帝没有其他直系男嗣。

sentences.en: And it must have symbolized for people at the time in the empire an anxiety that indeed the storm clouds are gathering.
sentences.zh: 对于当时帝国的人民来说，这一定象征着一种焦虑，即暴风雨确实正在聚集。

sentences.en: Don't you think?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I think exactly both those things.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这两点完全都有。

sentences.en: I think, first of all, it's a huge shock for the dynasty because, as you say, he doesn't have another son.
sentences.zh: 首先我认为这对皇朝来说是一个巨大的打击，因为正如你所说，他没有第二个儿子。

sentences.en: So they're going to have to search elsewhere in the family tree for an heir.
sentences.zh: 所以他们将不得不在家族树的其他地方寻找继承人。

sentences.en: Of course, the man that they find turns out to be a great friend of the rest is history, but a slightly ill-fated figure in his own right,
sentences.zh: 当然，他们找到的那个人后来成了“历史余音”节目的好朋友，但在他自己身上却是一个命运稍显悲惨的人物，

sentences.en: although the bird population of Central Europe might not agree.
sentences.zh: 尽管中欧的鸟类种群可能并不同意这一点。

sentences.en: And I think you're dead right.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为你完全说得对。

sentences.en: The cultural atmosphere of Fantasie, actually Vienna, the sense of neurosis, the sense of introspection, of cultural anxiety, also cultural excitement, of course.
sentences.zh: 《芬式世纪》中维也纳的文化氛围，那种神经质、内省感、文化焦虑，当然还有文化兴奋感。

sentences.en: And also the German-speaking world more generally, because Wagner is, I mean, you know, the Lieberstadt, the idea of love and death.
sentences.zh: 还有更广泛的德语世界，因为瓦格纳，我的意思是，你知道的，爱与死（Liebestod）的概念。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And two lovers who are united in death.
sentences.zh: 以及两个在死后结合的恋人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Tristan and Isolde.
sentences.zh: 《特里斯坦与伊索尔德》。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, it's probably the most celebrated work of music that has been produced in the late 19th century.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可能是19世纪末产生的最著名的音乐作品。

sentences.en: And, you know, we've seen how much a part it is of the kind of cultural furniture of people of this age.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们已经看到它在这个时代的人们的文化构件中占了多么大的比重。

sentences.en: It must just be overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 那一定让人感到无比震撼。

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: And precisely because it's so overwhelming, that's where you get the conspiracy theorists.
sentences.zh: 正因为它是如此震撼，所以阴谋论才会应运而生。

sentences.en: So we talked about this with the Kennedy assassination, with lots of things.
sentences.zh: 我们在谈论肯尼迪遇刺案以及很多事情时都讨论过这一点。

sentences.en: What appears to be a freak event, if it's seen by the public as cataclysmic and of seismic importance, people will often refuse to accept.
sentences.zh: 如果一件表面上看似离奇的事件被公众视为具有灾难性和震撼性的重大意义，人们往往会拒绝接受。

sentences.en: They don't like chance, luck, you know, personal quirks in history.
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢历史中的偶然性、运气和个人怪癖。

sentences.en: Great events must have great causes.
sentences.zh: 伟大的事件必然有伟大的原因。

sentences.en: And so people look for conspiracy theories that are related to the political anxieties of the day.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们会去寻找与当下的政治焦虑相关的阴谋论。

sentences.en: So people say, I mean, first of all, there are the sort of more humdrum conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 所以人们会说，我的意思是，首先是一些比较平庸的阴谋论。

sentences.en: Mary murdered Rudolph or her relatives murdered Rudolph, perhaps because they found out he'd given her gonorrhea and they wanted to punish him for it.
sentences.zh: 玛丽谋杀了鲁道夫，或者是她的亲属谋杀了鲁道夫，也许是因为他们发现鲁道夫把淋病传染给了她，并想因此惩罚他。

sentences.en: What about Stephanie?
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬妮怎么样？

sentences.en: Yeah, there are theories that Grand Princess Stephanie did it because she was jealous, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，有各种理论认为皇储妃斯蒂芬妮是凶手，因为她嫉妒，当然还有共济会、耶稣会、犹太人、俾斯麦干的。

sentences.en: The Freemasons, the Jesuits, the Jews, Bismarck did it.
sentences.zh: 不是德皇。

sentences.en: Not the Kaiser.
sentences.zh: 德皇？

sentences.en: The Kaiser?
sentences.zh: 不，有理论认为是德皇干的。

sentences.en: No, there are theories that the Kaiser did it.
sentences.zh: 但最常见、最多人说的——这显然反映了当时的政治氛围——这个理论真是太诡异了。

sentences.en: But the most common, the most, and this obviously reflects the political atmosphere of the day, that, I mean, this is such a weird theory.
sentences.zh: 他自杀或被谋杀是因为他即将被揭发，他曾策划从他父亲手中夺取匈牙利王位，与他父亲决裂，并建立一个分裂出去的匈牙利王国。

sentences.en: He either killed himself or was murdered because he was about to be exposed as having plotted to seize the throne of Hungary from his father and break away from his father and set up a secessionist Hungarian kingdom.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想这表达了父子之间显然存在的深刻紧张关系。

sentences.en: Well, I guess that's expressive of what is clearly a deep sense of tension between father and son.
sentences.zh: 但也是帝国两个部分之间的紧张关系。

sentences.en: But also between the two halves of the empire.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且你知道的，皇帝甚至在他儿子自杀的那天都对此念念不忘。

sentences.en: Yeah, and he's, you know, the emperor is obsessing about this even on the day of his son's suicide.
sentences.zh: 难道不是有一个由末代皇后齐塔提出的理论吗，说是法国人干的，是由克列孟梭策划的？

sentences.en: Isn't there a theory that was proposed by Empress Zeta, who was the last empress, that it was the French and that it had been organized by Clemenceau,
sentences.zh: 我认为人们普遍认为这不太可能。

sentences.en: which I think is generally not regarded as plausible.
sentences.zh: 克列孟梭为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: Why did Clemenceau do it?
sentences.zh: 提醒我一下，克列孟梭为什么要杀鲁道夫皇储？

sentences.en: Remind me why Clemenceau wanted to kill Grand Prince Rudolph?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我甚至觉得，他当时甚至都不在议会里。

sentences.en: Well, he wasn't even, I think, he wasn't even in parliament at this time.
sentences.zh: 我想那是她瞎编的，但她活到了一把年纪。

sentences.en: I think she made it up, but she lived to a kind of ripe old age.
sentences.zh: 我想她大概在70年代左右去世的吧。

sentences.en: I think she kind of died in the 70s or something.
sentences.zh: 确实是的。

sentences.en: She did, yeah.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能是80年代。

sentences.en: Maybe even the 80s.
sentences.zh: 而她一直在重复这个说法。

sentences.en: And she kept repeating this.
sentences.zh: 我不得不承认，我表现出了海格力斯般的自制力，没有在网上掉进各种匪夷所思的陷阱里，因为网上有太多人们关于这方面的讨论了。

sentences.en: I have to admit, I showed Herculean self-control by not falling down lots of rabbit holes online because there's so much stuff online about this by people.
sentences.zh: 因为人们喜欢茜茜公主，也喜欢鲁道夫皇储。

sentences.en: Because people love Cece and they love Grand Prince Rudolph.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你去卡普钦皇家墓穴，那里有所有哈布斯堡家族成员的陵墓。

sentences.en: So if you go to the Capuchin crypt, they have tombs of all the Habsburgs.
sentences.zh: 其中一些是巨头级别的人物。

sentences.en: And some of these are like massive figures.
sentences.zh: 比如玛丽亚·特蕾西亚什么的。

sentences.en: I don't know, Maria Theresa or something.
sentences.zh: 但鲁道夫皇储的墓上有更多的花，有非常多的花，要知道，他生前从未掌握过实权。

sentences.en: But Crown Prince Rudolph's tomb has more flowers, has a lot of flowers, you know, given that he never wielded power.
sentences.zh: 事实上，从宏观角度来看，你可以说他并不是一个至关重要的人物。

sentences.en: And actually, in the grand scheme of things, you could argue it's not a terribly consequential person.
sentences.zh: 但他的故事中显然有什么东西能够引发人们的共鸣，即使在21世纪的今天也是如此。

sentences.en: But there's clearly something about his story that speaks to people, even today in the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 他有点像是奥匈帝国的科特·柯本。

sentences.en: It's kind of Kurt Cobain of Austro-Hungary.
sentences.zh: 我是说，从它的政治意义来谈的话。

sentences.en: I mean, to talk about the political meaning of it.
sentences.zh: 任何撰写关于奥匈帝国或哈布斯堡王朝历史的史学家，你懂的，都会对这一点大书特书，这是可以理解的。

sentences.en: Any historian writing about the Austro-Hungarian Empire or the Habsburgs, you know, gives this a lot of welly, understandably.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是帝国大业更广泛丧失信心的症状。

sentences.en: And they see it as symptomatic of this wider loss of confidence of the imperial project.
sentences.zh: 这就是泰坦尼克号。

sentences.en: It's the Titanic.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 但就像泰坦尼克号一样，我认为这里面很大一部分被严重夸大了。

sentences.en: But as with the Titanic, I think a lot of this is massively overblown.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道玛丽和鲁道夫为什么要自杀。

sentences.en: So we know why Mary and Rudolph killed themselves.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他心理病态。

sentences.en: I mean, he's morbid.
sentences.zh: 他得了淋病。

sentences.en: He's got gonorrhea.
sentences.zh: 放在今天，他会被诊断出患有非常严重的心理健康问题。

sentences.en: Today, he would be diagnosed as having mental health issues of a very serious kind.
sentences.zh: 这确实说明了一个真正的问题，那就是生在哈布斯堡王朝就意味着感到被困住。

sentences.en: That does speak of something that is genuine, which is the way in which to be born into the Habsburg dynasty is to feel trapped.
sentences.zh: 感觉自己像个囚犯。

sentences.en: It's to feel a prisoner.
sentences.zh: 我们有关于男女两性几乎把自己缝进军服和衣服里的种种记载。

sentences.en: We have all these counts of both men and women almost sewing themselves into their uniforms and their clothing.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，弗朗茨·斐迪南大公被枪击时，他们花了很长时间才意识到鲜血正涌出来。

sentences.en: So, you know, Franz Ferdinand, when he gets shot, it takes time for them to realize that the blood is welling out.
sentences.zh: 我想我们接下来也会听到关于茜茜公主类似的说法。

sentences.en: We're going to hear something similar about Sisi in due course, I think.
sentences.zh: 但确实，对那些身处其中的人来说，君主制就是一种牢笼。

sentences.en: But there is that monarchy is a kind of trap for those who find themselves enclosed within it.
sentences.zh: 非常21世纪的主题，对吧？

sentences.en: Very 21st century theme, right?
sentences.zh: 人们经常说温莎王室也是这样，不是吗？

sentences.en: And people often say that's about the House of Windsor, don't they?
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 但温莎王室的不同之处在于，他们可以就此制作广播节目，还可以在报纸上发表谈论心理健康问题的专栏，

sentences.en: But the difference with the House of Windsor is that they can kind of make radio programs about it and kind of have features in newspapers talking about bad mental health,
sentences.zh: 而鲁道夫则不能。

sentences.en: whereas Rudolph couldn't.
sentences.zh: 而且让这些皇室成员真正拥有某种内心情感生活的想法是绝对禁止的。

sentences.en: And the idea of any of these people really having a kind of interior emotional life is verboten.
sentences.zh: 不过有趣的是，在他之前居然没有人这么做过，不是吗？

sentences.en: Interesting that nobody had done this before him, though, no?
sentences.zh: 这说明了什么？

sentences.en: What does that tell you?
sentences.zh: 19世纪下半叶发生了一些变化，才使得这种事情成为可能。

sentences.en: Something changed in the second half of the 19th century that made this possible.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很难想象一个14世纪的王子会这样做。

sentences.en: I mean, it's hard to imagine a 14th century prince.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且没有什么地方比维也纳更能体现这种变化了。

sentences.en: No, and it's changing nowhere more than in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 没错，完全如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 维也纳是——你知道的，压抑、神经症、精神病以及种种概念正是在这个特定时刻被定义的。

sentences.en: Vienna is the, you know, this is where all these ideas of repression and neurosis and psychosis and everything are being defined at this very moment.
sentences.zh: 也许是一种特殊的内省以及对自我的感知，或者我不知道。

sentences.en: Maybe a particular kind of introspection and a sense of yourself or I don't know.
sentences.zh: 他在“氛围摆烂”，我想这是这个词吧。

sentences.en: He's vibe lording, I believe it's the phrase.
sentences.zh: 这是在摆出某种氛围。

sentences.en: It's vibe lording.
sentences.zh: 是这个词吗？

sentences.en: Is that the phrase?

sentences.en: Gen Z joins us on the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: So what happened next?
sentences.zh: 弗朗茨·约瑟夫——我的意思是，这非常弗洛伊德，弗雷德里克·莫顿在他的书中也提出了这一点。

sentences.en: Franz Joseph, I mean, this is very Freudian and Frederick Morton makes this point in his book.
sentences.zh: 他想要抹去关于这一事件的每一丝痕迹、每一段记忆。

sentences.en: He wants to erase every trace, every memory of this incident.
sentences.zh: 他做到这一点的方式就是从字面上抹去那个地方。

sentences.en: And the way he does it is by literally erasing the place.
sentences.zh: 所以梅林堡的狩猎小屋，它的每一处痕迹都被从地球上抹去了。

sentences.en: So the hunting lodge at Myerling, every trace of it is expunged from the earth.
sentences.zh: 它被彻底拆毁，并取而代之建立了一座加尔默罗会修道院，至今犹存。

sentences.en: It's completely pulled down and it is replaced with a Carmelite convent, which stands to this day.
sentences.zh: 修道院的修女们被嘱咐要每天为已故皇储的灵魂祈祷。

sentences.en: And the nuns of the convent are enjoined to offer daily prayers for the salvation of the late crown prince.
sentences.zh: 他需要所有他能得到的祈祷。

sentences.en: He needs all the prayers he can get.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 所以弗朗茨·约瑟夫现在最有可能的继承人是他的弟弟卡尔·路德维希，当时他已经快六十岁了。

sentences.en: So the most likely heir to Franz Joseph now is his younger brother, Karl Ludwig, who is in his late 50s.
sentences.zh: 但卡尔·路德维希的健康状况并不算太好。

sentences.en: But Karl Ludwig's not in brilliant health.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪90年代末，即1896年，他去巴勒斯坦进行了一次朝圣，当时巴勒斯坦是奥斯曼帝国的一部分。

sentences.en: And in the late 1890s, in 1896, he went on a sort of pilgrimage to Palestine, then part of the Ottoman Empire.
sentences.zh: 他决定喝一些约旦河的水。

sentences.en: And he decided to drink some water from the River Jordan.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是喝了被污水污染的脏水。

sentences.en: He basically drank dirty water polluted with sewage.
sentences.zh: 所以痢疾又回到了我们的节目中吗？

sentences.en: So do we get his dysentery returned to the show?
sentences.zh: 痢疾重返节目，并夺走了卡尔·路德维希的生命。

sentences.en: Dysentery returned to the show and carried off Karl Ludwig.
sentences.zh: 痢疾再次在这个节目中爆发，并夺走了卡尔·路易斯的生命。

sentences.en: And the heir became his son, Rudolf's protégé, Franz Ferdinand.
sentences.zh: 而继承人成了他的儿子、鲁道프的门生弗兰茨·斐迪南。

sentences.en: So a great friend of the rest is history, but we know what became of him.
sentences.zh: 所以《余下皆历史》的其他内容众所周知，但我们知道他的结局如何。

sentences.en: And actually, this brings us to the wider issue of tragedy in the Habsburgs.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这也让我们想到了哈布斯堡家族更广泛的悲剧问题。

sentences.en: So you've already alluded to this.
sentences.zh: 所以你已经暗示过这一点了。

sentences.en: In the decade after Rudolf's death, his mother Cece cut an ever more, ever lonelier, more melancholy figure.
sentences.zh: 在鲁道夫死后的十年里，他的母亲茜茜显得越来越孤独、越来越忧郁。

sentences.en: So she basically, she's dressed always in black in mourning for her son.
sentences.zh: 所以她基本上总是穿着黑衣，为她的儿子服丧。

sentences.en: And she drifts around the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 她在地中海一带四处漂泊。

sentences.en: She's thinner than ever.
sentences.zh: 她比以往任何时候都瘦。

sentences.en: She looks very sad, you know, solitary.
sentences.zh: 她看起来非常悲伤，你知道的，形单影只。

sentences.en: And in autumn of 1898, she was staying at Lake Geneva.
sentences.zh: 1898年秋天，她正住在日内瓦湖畔。

sentences.en: And Franz Joseph, her husband, was still writing to her all the time from Vienna.
sentences.zh: 而她的丈夫弗兰茨·约瑟夫仍然一直在维也纳给她写信。

sentences.en: And he would write these very sweet letters.
sentences.zh: 他会写下这些非常甜蜜的信。

sentences.en: The end of one letter, he signs off.
sentences.zh: 在一封信的结尾，他落款署名。

sentences.en: He says, sort of, farewell, my most beautiful, my best and sweetest angel.
sentences.zh: 他写道，再见吧，我最美丽、最好、最甜美的小天使。

sentences.en: But the sad thing is she never got to read this particular letter.
sentences.zh: 但悲哀的是，她至死也没能读到这封特别的信。

sentences.en: Because while it was en route, on the 10th of September, 1898, she was boarding the steamer to Montreux on Lake Geneva, which just had one lady waiting with her.
sentences.zh: 因为就在信件在途中时，即1898年9月10日，她正登上日内瓦湖开往蒙特勒的轮船，当时只有一个女伴在等她。

sentences.en: And she was standing amid the crush of people when suddenly she collapsed.
sentences.zh: 她正站在拥挤的人群中，突然她倒下了。

sentences.en: And no one could work out why she collapsed at firSt.
sentences.zh: 起初谁也没有弄明白她为什么会倒下。

sentences.en: As you said, she's very tightly sewn into her corset.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，她的紧身胸衣勒得非常紧。

sentences.en: And when finally they worked out what happened, they realized that she had been stabbed through the heart with a sharpened stiletto, a kind of improvised stiletto.
sentences.zh: 当他们最终弄清楚发生了什么时，才意识到她的心脏被一把削尖的细长匕首刺穿了，那是一种自制的匕首。

sentences.en: By an Italian anarchist called Luigi Lucchini.
sentences.zh: 凶手是一名叫路易吉·卢凯尼的意大利无政府主义者。

sentences.en: And he had traveled to Geneva to kill a royal, because it was a favorite royal hangout.
sentences.zh: 他去日内瓦是为了杀死一名皇室成员，因为那是皇室成员最喜欢的聚集地。

sentences.en: And he said afterwards he didn't care which one he killed as long as he killed one.
sentences.zh: 他事后说，他不在乎杀的是哪一个，只要能杀一个就行。

sentences.en: And Sisi was the person that he killed.
sentences.zh: 而茜茜就是他杀的那个人。

sentences.en: And when the news got back to Vienna, Franz Joseph, apparently when he heard the news, he sobbed uncontrollably.
sentences.zh: 当消息传回维也纳时，据说弗兰茨·约瑟夫听到这个消息后痛哭失声。

sentences.en: And then he said to one of his aides, so I am to be spared nothing in this world.
sentences.zh: 然后他对他的一个助手说，难道在这个世界上没有什么痛苦是可以放过我的吗？

sentences.en: Nobody knows the love we had for each other.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道我们彼此深爱至深。

sentences.en: It's a sort of bitterly ironic thing for him to say.
sentences.zh: 对他说这样的话来说，真是一种充满苦涩讽刺的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this for him was the crowning blow.
sentences.zh: 所以对维也纳来说，这就是沉重打击的顶峰。

sentences.en: He still had his actress, Katerina Schratz, though their relationship had actually cooled by this point.
sentences.zh: 他依然有他的女演员卡塔琳娜·施拉茨，尽管此时他们的关系实际上已经变冷了。

sentences.en: He's very lonely.
sentences.zh: 他非常孤独。

sentences.en: He writes to Katerina Schratz at one point.
sentences.zh: 他曾在某个时刻写信给卡塔琳娜·施拉茨。

sentences.en: I feel endlessly sad in my hopeless loneliness.
sentences.zh: 我在无望的孤独中感到无尽的悲伤。

sentences.en: His son has killed himself.
sentences.zh: 他的儿子自杀了。

sentences.en: His wife has been murdered.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子被谋杀了。

sentences.en: He's effectively on his own.

sentences.en: And he lives for another 18 years after his wife's death.

sentences.en: It seems incredibly old at this point.

sentences.en: He actually looks older than he is.

sentences.en: But at this point, he looked about 150.
sentences.zh: 但当时他看起来大约有150岁。

sentences.en: And people talked about him as a relic at this point.
sentences.zh: 当时人们把他当作一件历史遗物来谈论。

sentences.en: They would call him the last knight or the old gentleman or something.
sentences.zh: 他们会叫他最后的骑士或是老绅士之类的。

sentences.en: And he remains enormously popular, Franz Joseph, a great rallying point for his empire.
sentences.zh: 弗兰茨·约瑟夫依然享有巨大的声望，是其帝国的巨大凝聚力所在。

sentences.en: And his suffering actually worked quite well as a political asset because the papers would call him the man of sorrows, sort of a man who has lost everything, wife, son, you know,
sentences.zh: 他的痛苦实际上作为政治资产发挥了相当不错的作用，因为报纸会称他为多灾多难的人，一个失去了一切的人，妻子，儿子，你知道的，

sentences.en: all the light has gone from his life.
sentences.zh: 生命中的所有光芒都已消逝。

sentences.en: And yet still he dedicates himself every day, gets up at four o'clock in the morning, his red boxes, to the peoples of his empire.
sentences.zh: 然而他每天仍然致力于帝国的人民，每天早晨四点起床，处理他的红皮文件箱。

sentences.en: But I suppose another way of looking at it is precisely because he is such a relic.
sentences.zh: 但我想换个角度来看，恰恰是因为他是个如此古老的遗物。

sentences.en: He seems like the embodiment of an antiquated institutional conservatism,
sentences.zh: 他看起来像是陈旧的制度保守主义的化身，

sentences.en: an empire that seems utterly beleaguered by the modern world and an empire that feels itself to be so embattled.
sentences.zh: 一个在现代世界中显得四面楚歌、感到自己深陷重围的帝国。
